title: 2023 HMMT November Guts Problem 23
statement: The points \(A=\left(4, \frac{1}{4}\right)\) and \(B=\left(-5,-\frac{1}{5}\right)\) lie on the hyperbola \(x y=1\). The circle with diameter \(A B\) intersects this hyperbola again at points \(X\) and \(Y\). Compute \(X Y\).

solutions.text:
Let \(A=(a, 1 / a), B=(b, \underline{1 / b})\), and \(X=(x, 1 / x)\). Since \(X\) lies on the circle with diameter \(\overline{A B}\), we have \(\angle A X B=90^{\circ}\). Thus, \(\overline{A X}\) and \(\overline{B X}\) are perpendicular, and so the product of their slopes must be -1 . We deduce:

\[\frac{a-x}{\frac{1}{a}-\frac{1}{x}} \frac{b-x}{\frac{1}{b}-\frac{1}{x}}=-1 \Longrightarrow(a x)(b x)=-1\]

so \(x= \pm \sqrt{-a b}\). Plugging in \(a=4\) and \(b=-5\) gives \(X=(\sqrt{20}, 1 / \sqrt{20})\) and \(Y=(-\sqrt{20},-1 / \sqrt{20})\), giving the answer.
